The objectives are pursued with the support of the Internationalisation Service (SI) and the International Cooperation Development Sector (ISDN) , which act in accordance with the Commission for International Relations of the University. The activities are carried out, although within the framework of the competences of the respective Areas, in a framework of collaboration, exchange of information flows and integration, in close contact with the delegates for internationalisation of the Departments and Schools and with the International Relations Commission . With reference to the overall framework of funding, projects and actions foreseen by the Erasmus+ Community Programme, the competences are divided as follows: Erasmus+ Programme Actions Office KA 1: Learning mobility of individuals SI KA 2.1 Strategic Partnerships in education, training and youth SI KA 2.2 Knowledge Alliances SSCI KA 2.3 Sector Skills alliances SSCI KA 2.4 Capacity Building in the field of higher education SSCI KA 2.5 Capacity Building in the field of youth SSCI KA 3: Support for Policy Reform SSCI Jean Monnet SI The conclusion of bilateral cooperation agreements between the University of Genoa and higher education institutes of Member States and Partner Countries is desired by the Government bodies and promoted, in the manner described below, both by the core structures and by the two Support Services. The purpose of these agreements is to initiate cooperation for the carrying out of integrated teaching and scientific activities, for the development of integrated study programmes for students and for the implementation of joint cooperation projects promoted by the competent Community Agencies in the field of Higher Education and Culture. List of academic cooperation agreements by the Internationalisation Service (updated 04.08.2025) Procedure for stipulation In order to proceed with the stipulation of an academic cooperation agreement: the lecturer proposes to the Internationalisation Service ( relint@unige.it ) or to the International Cooperation Development Office ( intstrat@unige.it ) the academic cooperation agreement, accompanied by a synthetic project plan containing the main aims, the reasons for the choice of the partner(s) and, in the case of more than one partner, the specification of the role played by each the offices ascertain the legal status of the potential partner university and any variations to the standard UniGe agreement text made by it the proposing professor shares the final agreement text with the Delegate for International Relations of his/her Department, by sending an email in which the central office of reference ( relint@unige.it or intstrat@unige.it ) the office involved submits the proposal to the International Relations Commission, including the ascertainment of legal status and the observations regarding any variations in the text if the International Relations Commission accepts the proposal, the offices inform the proposing professor and proceed with the acquisition of the Rector's signature. Once signed, the agreement will be sent to the partner for countersignature. Once both parties have signed, the Delegate for International Relations, duly informed by the offices, shall inform the Department Council if the International Relations Commission expresses reservations regarding the proposal, the proposing professor shall be called upon to provide further clarifications in order to have more elements for evaluation. Schemes of academic cooperation agreement type Italian version English version French version Spanish version Schemes of academic cooperation agreement accompanied by the Executive Programme for Implementation (PEI) The adoption of the PEI is suggested in the case of agreements for which the proposers have already defined subjects and topics to be covered in the short to medium term by application to the European Commission, joint publications and research, Summer School . Italian version English version French version Spanish version Type of mobility implementation agreement The stipulation of an academic cooperation agreement may be preliminary or concomitant to the stipulation of an implementation mobility agreement focused on the exchange of teachers and/or students at University, School or Department level. The mobility implementation agreement may also be proposed outside an academic cooperation agreement, provided that it is supported by a solid project plan. It must, however, include the fundamental clauses (e.g.: safety, insurance). Italian version English version French version spanish version Type of academic cooperation mobility agreement This type of agreement has been drawn up to allow individual teaching facilities to sign agreements with homologous foreign facilities in order to initiate mobility both of students and of teaching and technical-administrative staff. With reference to the overall framework of funding, projects and actions foreseen by the Erasmus+ Community Programme, the competences are divided as follows: Erasmus+ Programme Actions Office KA 1: Learning mobility of individuals SI KA 2.1 Strategic Partnerships in education, training and youth SI KA 2.2 Knowledge Alliances SSCI KA 2.3 Sector Skills alliances SSCI KA 2.4 Capacity Building in the field of higher education SSCI KA 2.5 Capacity Building in the field of youth SSCI KA 3: Support for Policy Reform SSCI Jean Monnet SI The conclusion of bilateral cooperation agreements between the University of Genoa and higher education institutes of Member States and Partner Countries is desired by the Government bodies and promoted, in the manner described below, both by the core structures and by the two Support Services. The purpose of these agreements is to initiate cooperation for the carrying out of integrated teaching and scientific activities, for the development of integrated study programmes for students and for the implementation of joint cooperation projects promoted by the competent Community Agencies in the field of Higher Education and Culture. List of academic cooperation agreements by the Internationalisation Service (updated 04.08.2025) Procedure for stipulation In order to proceed with the stipulation of an academic cooperation agreement: the lecturer proposes to the Internationalisation Service ( relint@unige.it ) or to the International Cooperation Development Office ( intstrat@unige.it ) the academic cooperation agreement, accompanied by a synthetic project plan containing the main aims, the reasons for the choice of the partner(s) and, in the case of more than one partner, the specification of the role played by each the offices ascertain the legal status of the potential partner university and any variations to the standard UniGe agreement text made by it the proposing professor shares the final agreement text with the Delegate for International Relations of his/her Department, by sending an email in which the central office of reference ( relint@unige.it or intstrat@unige.it ) the office involved submits the proposal to the International Relations Commission, including the ascertainment of legal status and the observations regarding any variations in the text if the International Relations Commission accepts the proposal, the offices inform the proposing professor and proceed with the acquisition of the Rector's signature. Once signed, the agreement will be sent to the partner for countersignature. Once both parties have signed, the Delegate for International Relations, duly informed by the offices, shall inform the Department Council if the International Relations Commission expresses reservations regarding the proposal, the proposing professor shall be called upon to provide further clarifications in order to have more elements for evaluation. Through cooperation with foreign institutions and entities, the University aims to increase educational, scientific and cultural exchanges. The International Cooperation Development Department is in charge of promoting and managing the following activities. Main activities Academic cooperation Academic cooperation with foreign universities and other institutions in order to: organise joint programmes and promote scholarships for research, education and training development in partner universities, increase international mobility of students and university staff, strengthen cooperation in the field of scientific research. The project is developed, in particular, through: the mobility of undergraduate and postgraduate students, lecturers, professors, researchers, technical and administrative staff, collaboration in activities of particular scientific interest, also through the sharing of experiences in the use of complex technical-scientific apparatus, cultural initiatives of common interest such as seminars, conferences and study meetings, development of initiatives aimed at improving governance and management, development of joint projects to be submitted for funding by the European Commission or other supranational organisations, actions aimed at the communication and dissemination of the knowledge acquired through the performance of the above activities. The establishment of cooperation agreements with foreign higher education institutions aimed at promoting collaboration for the development of integrated scientific activities and joint study programmes. Official agreement forms - with or without an implementation protocol - available in different languages. List of concluded cooperation agreements - procedure managed by the International Cooperation Department. International Cooperation Projects National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR) - Mission 4 'Education and Research': Transnational Educational Initiatives (TNE) The aim is to promote the internationalisation of Italian universities and to enhance the Italian higher education model as a best practice at international level. The two-year funded initiatives are aimed at non-EU contexts, with particular reference to areas of strategic interest including the non-EU countries of the Mediterranean, the Balkan Peninsula and the states of the African continent. The MUR, in agreement with MAECI, has focused on relations with Least Developed Countries. EU programme: ERASMUS+ Previous EU Programmes: Alpha III Erasmus Mundus Tempus Development and submission of applications for cooperation projects with institutions from EU Member States and partner countries, within the framework of programmes promoted by the European Commission. Management and implementation of the funded projects. Daily tasks: Management of the work plan of the projects. Organisation of project meetings to be held at UniGe or at partner institutions, training stages for delegations, intensive courses for JR teaching staff, mobility flows, etc. Dissemination and networking activities. Accounting and reporting activities. Through cooperation with foreign institutions and entities, the University aims to increase educational, scientific and cultural exchanges. The International Cooperation Development Department is in charge of promoting and managing the following activities. Main activities Academic cooperation Academic cooperation with foreign universities and other institutions in order to: organise joint programmes and promote scholarships for research, education and training development in partner universities, increase international mobility of students and university staff, strengthen cooperation in the field of scientific research. The project is developed, in particular, through: the mobility of undergraduate and postgraduate students, lecturers, professors, researchers, technical and administrative staff, collaboration in activities of particular scientific interest, also through the sharing of experiences in the use of complex technical-scientific apparatus, cultural initiatives of common interest such as seminars, conferences and study meetings, development of initiatives aimed at improving governance and management, development of joint projects to be submitted for funding by the European Commission or other supranational organisations, actions aimed at the communication and dissemination of the knowledge acquired through the performance of the above activities. The establishment of cooperation agreements with foreign higher education institutions aimed at promoting collaboration for the development of integrated scientific activities and joint study programmes. Official agreement forms - with or without an implementation protocol - available in different languages. List of concluded cooperation agreements - procedure managed by the International Cooperation Department. International Cooperation Projects National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR) - Mission 4 'Education and Research': Transnational Educational Initiatives (TNE) The aim is to promote the internationalisation of Italian universities and to enhance the Italian higher education model as a best practice at international level. The two-year funded initiatives are aimed at non-EU contexts, with particular reference to areas of strategic interest including the non-EU countries of the Mediterranean, the Balkan Peninsula and the states of the African continent. The MUR, in agreement with MAECI, has focused on relations with Least Developed Countries. EU programme: ERASMUS+ Previous EU Programmes: Alpha III Erasmus Mundus Tempus Development and submission of applications for cooperation projects with institutions from EU Member States and partner countries, within the framework of programmes promoted by the European Commission. Management and implementation of the funded projects. Daily tasks: Management of the work plan of the projects. Organisation of project meetings to be held at UniGe or at partner institutions, training stages for delegations, intensive courses for JR teaching staff, mobility flows, etc. Dissemination and networking activities. Accounting and reporting activities. UniGe ti offre la possibilità di partecipare a programmi di studio a doppio titolo , attivati in collaborazione con università straniere, per il rilascio della doppia laurea . Cos'è Il doppio titolo è un programma di studio integrato istituito con una o più università estere . Ti permette di frequentare una parte del tuo percorso universitario presso UniGe e una parte presso le università partner, ottenendo cosi un titolo riconosciuto in tutti i Paesi in cui hai studiato. Chi può partecipare Puoi partecipare se il tuo Corso prevede il percorso a doppio titolo. Scopri i corsi di UniGe che offrono questo programma internazionale e ti permettono di ottenere un titolo riconosciuto in Italia e nel paese in cui hai studiato. Quando Ogni anno accademico vengono svolte selezioni per l’ammissione ai singoli percorsi a doppio titolo. Come accedere Vuoi sapere se le mobilità previste dal doppio titolo sono finanziate e quali sono i requisiti specifici richiesti dai singoli percorsi? Visita la pagina dedicata per tenerti aggiornato. You can consult the document on the provisions in force in the a.a. 2025/26 here: institutional source Circular_2025-2026_international_students.pdf - Universitaly The Italian language and culture teaching activities proposed by the Language Skills Development Department are aimed at: international students of degree courses IN ENGLISH who do not have a curricular Italian course and students IN INTERNATIONAL MOBILITY international students enrolled at the University of Genoa on degree courses in English and who do not have an Italian course already scheduled in their study plan may attend an Italian course reserved for them, information about which can be found at https://clat.unige.it/italiano_dottorandi_mastercourses students on international mobility (Erasmus and other mobility projects - Cinda, etc.) can find information on Italian courses reserved for them on the page https://clat.unige.en/Incoming aspiring international students of the Italian courses see the dedicated section: Italian courses for aspiring international students Test of knowledge of the Italian language international students with a foreign degree and a degree in ITALIAN LANGUAGE with OFA find online the information for the test of knowledge of the Italian language aspiring international students with foreign qualifications who intend to enrol in a degree programme in ITALIAN LANGUAGE in the academic year 2026/2027 must take a test of knowledge of the Italian language in order to enrol Italian courses for international students with O.F.A. a.y. 2025/2026 Students enrolled at UniGe by 30 November 2025 Italian courses for international students enrolled in degree courses delivered in Italian are reserved exclusively for those who meet these requirements: resulted suitable for level A2 but not B2 in the tests delivered in the autumn session of the TEST TE.L.E.MA.CO. (September-November 2025) (see the dedicated session: Test of knowledge of the Italian language ) has enrolled (i.e. completed enrolment) in the first year in the a.a. 2025/26 by 30 November 2025. meets these requirements: Only students with these requirements receive an email from the Language Skills Development Department with instructions on how to attend the teacher-led Italian course in which they have been placed on the basis of their results in the B2 test. The courses last 40 hours or 80 hours (depending on the results of the test) and attendance is compulsory: you must attend at least 50% of the hours to be admitted to the final exam. You can attend the Italian course with a teacher only once and exclusively in the year of enrolment: no course is offered to students repeating the first year. As already mentioned, students who do not pass the exam that concludes the course will retake the Italian test starting on 25 June 2026 and, if they do not pass it again, on the dates listed in the dedicated session: Calendar of Italian tests for the academic year 2025/26 Approximately ten days before the test date, the Language Skills Development Sector sends an email to students invited to take the test; to find out if you are among those invited, write to the Welcome Office Sector: sass@unige.it Students enrolled at UniGe after 30 November 2025 Students who enrol at the University of Genoa (i.e. who complete their enrolment) after 30 November 2025 will only be able to request the activation of an online Italian course (self-study and without a teacher) at B1 or B2 level (based on the score obtained in the B2 test) by writing to clat@unige.it The online course is activated exclusively upon the student's request. Students who have enrolled after 30 November 2025 may retake the Italian test from 25 June 2026 ; if they fail, they may take it on the dates listed in the dedicated session: Calendar of Italian tests for the academic year 2025/26 Approximately ten days before the test date, the Language Skills Development Sector sends an email to students invited to take the test; to find out if you are among those invited, please write to the Welcome Office Sector: sass@unige.it All students with O.F.A. in Italian will be able to take the first-year exams , but will not be able to enrol in the second year until they have passed the Italian B2 test. Italian courses for aspiring international students a.y. 2026/2027 Italian courses for aspiring international students intending to enrol for the first time in the academic year 2026/2027 The University of Genoa offers a limited number of students two types of courses to support them in achieving the B2 Italian requirement at ministerial level; these courses are described below. 1. SUMMER PRE-CURSES 2026 online These pre-courses are reserved for: non-EU students residing abroad who have applied on UnigeApply by 1 April 2026 are in possession of an A2 or B1 Italian language certification obtained following an examination taken by 1 January 2024 and issued by the University for Foreigners of Perugia, the University for Foreigners of Siena, the University for Foreigners "Dante Alighieri" of Reggio Calabria and - limited to B1 level - by the Centro Studi Italiani of Urbania and to students resident in Italy who have been certified by the University for Foreigners of Siena;who were accepted on UnigeApply by 28 May 2026 are in possession of a certification of Italian B1 obtained following an examination taken since 1 January 2024 and issuedby the University for Foreigners of Perugia, by the University for Foreigners of Siena, by the University for Foreigners "Dante Alighieri" of Reggio Calabria and by the Centro Studi Italiani of Urbania. These courses will take place in onrubrline mode; information on how to participate will be communicated from April 2026 by the Language Skills Development Department exclusively to the names selected on the basis of the indications received by the Welcome Office Department on 1 April 2026 and 28 May 2026; the lessons will take place between May and August 2026 . 2. AUTUMNAL COURSES 2026 These courses are reserved for aspiring international students who take the B2 Italian language test administered by TEST TE.L.E.MA.CO. on 14-15-16 September 2026 or the Italian language test administered by the Language Skills Development Sector on 17 September 2026 and have achieved an adequate score, even if lower than B2, established by the Language Skills Development Sector and which will be communicated shortly. Only these aspiring students will receive an email from the Language Skills Development Department with the information to participate in the Italian B2 courses organised by the University of Genoa, which will be held approximately from mid-September to mid-November and they will be able to repeat the Italian B2 test on 18 November 2026 with the TEST TE.L.E.MA.CO. or on 19 November 2026 with the Language Skills Development ; if they do not pass, they will not be able to enrol in any degree course at the University of Genoa taught in Italian. IMPORTANT : those who take the Italian B2 test on the dates of the TE.L.E.MA.CO. test after the above-mentioned dates or the Italian B2 test on dates after 17 September will NOT be offered any Italian courses and will not be able to retake the test. Read the new provisions for uploading Italian certificates for the academic year 2026/2027 Proficiency in Italian is not required in the case of courses delivered in English. Important notice for those who will enrol in 2026/27 In the academic year 2026/27 it will be compulsory to have a B2 level knowledge of Italian at the time of enrolment, as per ministerial regulations. You can consult the document on the provisions in force in the a.a. 2025/26 here: institutional source Circular_2025-2026_international_students.pdf - Universitaly The Italian language and culture teaching activities proposed by the Language Skills Development Department are aimed at: international students of degree courses IN ENGLISH who do not have a curricular Italian course and students IN INTERNATIONAL MOBILITY international students enrolled at the University of Genoa on degree courses in English and who do not have an Italian course already scheduled in their study plan may attend an Italian course reserved for them, information about which can be found at https://clat.unige.it/italiano_dottorandi_mastercourses students on international mobility (Erasmus and other mobility projects - Cinda, etc.) can find information on Italian courses reserved for them on the page https://clat.unige.en/Incoming aspiring international students of the Italian courses see the dedicated section: Italian courses for aspiring international students Test of knowledge of the Italian language international students with a foreign degree and a degree in ITALIAN LANGUAGE with OFA find online the information for the test of knowledge of the Italian language aspiring international students with foreign qualifications who intend to enrol in a degree programme in ITALIAN LANGUAGE in the academic year 2026/2027 must take a test of knowledge of the Italian language in order to enrol Italian courses for international students with O.F.A. a.y. 2025/2026 Students enrolled at UniGe by 30 November 2025 Italian courses for international students enrolled in degree courses delivered in Italian are reserved exclusively for those who meet these requirements: resulted suitable for level A2 but not B2 in the tests delivered in the autumn session of the TEST TE.L.E.MA.CO. (September-November 2025) (see the dedicated session: Test of knowledge of the Italian language ) has enrolled (i.e. completed enrolment) in the first year in the a.a. 2025/26 by 30 November 2025. meets these requirements: Only students with these requirements receive an email from the Language Skills Development Department with instructions on how to attend the teacher-led Italian course in which they have been placed on the basis of their results in the B2 test. The courses last 40 hours or 80 hours (depending on the results of the test) and attendance is compulsory: you must attend at least 50% of the hours to be admitted to the final exam. You can attend the Italian course with a teacher only once and exclusively in the year of enrolment: no course is offered to students repeating the first year. As already mentioned, students who do not pass the exam that concludes the course will retake the Italian test starting on 25 June 2026 and, if they do not pass it again, on the dates listed in the dedicated session: Calendar of Italian tests for the academic year 2025/26 Approximately ten days before the test date, the Language Skills Development Sector sends an email to students invited to take the test; to find out if you are among those invited, write to the Welcome Office Sector: sass@unige.it Students enrolled at UniGe after 30 November 2025 Students who enrol at the University of Genoa (i.e. who complete their enrolment) after 30 November 2025 will only be able to request the activation of an online Italian course (self-study and without a teacher) at B1 or B2 level (based on the score obtained in the B2 test) by writing to clat@unige.it The online course is activated exclusively upon the student's request. Students who have enrolled after 30 November 2025 may retake the Italian test from 25 June 2026 ; if they fail, they may take it on the dates listed in the dedicated session: Calendar of Italian tests for the academic year 2025/26 Approximately ten days before the test date, the Language Skills Development Sector sends an email to students invited to take the test; to find out if you are among those invited, please write to the Welcome Office Sector: sass@unige.it All students with O.F.A. in Italian will be able to take the first-year exams , but will not be able to enrol in the second year until they have passed the Italian B2 test. Italian courses for aspiring international students a.y. 2026/2027 Italian courses for aspiring international students intending to enrol for the first time in the academic year 2026/2027 The University of Genoa offers a limited number of students two types of courses to support them in achieving the B2 Italian requirement at ministerial level; these courses are described below. 1. SUMMER PRE-CURSES 2026 online These pre-courses are reserved for: non-EU students residing abroad who have applied on UnigeApply by 1 April 2026 are in possession of an A2 or B1 Italian language certification obtained following an examination taken by 1 January 2024 and issued by the University for Foreigners of Perugia, the University for Foreigners of Siena, the University for Foreigners "Dante Alighieri" of Reggio Calabria and - limited to B1 level - by the Centro Studi Italiani of Urbania and to students resident in Italy who have been certified by the University for Foreigners of Siena;who were accepted on UnigeApply by 28 May 2026 are in possession of a certification of Italian B1 obtained following an examination taken since 1 January 2024 and issuedby the University for Foreigners of Perugia, by the University for Foreigners of Siena, by the University for Foreigners "Dante Alighieri" of Reggio Calabria and by the Centro Studi Italiani of Urbania. These courses will take place in onrubrline mode; information on how to participate will be communicated from April 2026 by the Language Skills Development Department exclusively to the names selected on the basis of the indications received by the Welcome Office Department on 1 April 2026 and 28 May 2026; the lessons will take place between May and August 2026 . 2. AUTUMNAL COURSES 2026 These courses are reserved for aspiring international students who take the B2 Italian language test administered by TEST TE.L.E.MA.CO. on 14-15-16 September 2026 or the Italian language test administered by the Language Skills Development Sector on 17 September 2026 and have achieved an adequate score, even if lower than B2, established by the Language Skills Development Sector and which will be communicated shortly. Only these aspiring students will receive an email from the Language Skills Development Department with the information to participate in the Italian B2 courses organised by the University of Genoa, which will be held approximately from mid-September to mid-November and they will be able to repeat the Italian B2 test on 18 November 2026 with the TEST TE.L.E.MA.CO. or on 19 November 2026 with the Language Skills Development ; if they do not pass, they will not be able to enrol in any degree course at the University of Genoa taught in Italian. IMPORTANT : those who take the Italian B2 test on the dates of the TE.L.E.MA.CO. test after the above-mentioned dates or the Italian B2 test on dates after 17 September will NOT be offered any Italian courses and will not be able to retake the test. Please note that students with a foreign diploma obtained in Italy from one of the following Institutions are exempt from applying to Unigeapply: International School of Genoa; Deledda International School (Genoa); Scuola Germanica Genova (Deutsche Schule Genua). CALL OPENING CLOSING CLOSED SELECTION Fall session - selection for visa applicant students 26th November 2025 20th March 2026 OPEN SELECTION Spring session - selection for resident students (*) 9th April 2026 for access to master's degrees: 28th August 2026(**) for bachelor's degree and single-cycle 5-6 year degrees: 25th September 2026(**) (*) Italian and EU citizens (wherever resident) and non-EU citizens already legally in Italy. (**) Please note, in case of courses with scheduled access: dedicated closure based on the call, the student will be able to apply on Unigeapply within two weeks prior to the last date of registration for the entrance test. FALL SESSION - EARLY SELECTION CLOSURES ONLY for the courses listed below because the target number of positively selected students is about to be reached: Fall session - selection for visa applicant students, MEDICAL PHARMACEUTICAL BIOTECHNOLOGY (Master's degree taught in English) course closes 13 th February 2026; Fall session - selection for visa applicant students, MARITIME SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY (Bachelor's degree taught in English) course closes 18 th February 2026; Fall session - selection for visa applicant students, COMPUTER ENGINEERING (Bachelor's degree taught in English) course closes 8 th March 2026; CONSULT ALL INFORMATION The services offered on Unige Online Services Always consult the opening and closing dates of services . To access the services, you must register and obtain UniGePass credentials. The credentials obtained are valid for accessing all services, always use the same ones. Registration: obtaining UniGePass credentials for accessing Unige Online Services (if you are already a registered user, use the credentials you already have) > go to the service UniGeApply: application submission > go to the service Pre-enrollment: submission of application (only following an approved application on Unigeapply and, in the case of visa-applying students, an approved application also on Universitaly) > go to the service Uploading the Italian language certificate for final verification (for free access courses taught in Italian) > go to the service Visa applicant students: upload final documentation to finalize the enrollment (only following a submitted pre-enrollment application) > go to the service Resident students (non-visa applicants): upload final documentation to finalize enrollment (only following a submitted pre-enrollment application) > go to the service Enrollment: confirmation of pre-enrollment (only following approval of the documentation provided and, for access to master's degrees, final approval of the course of study) > go to the service A.Y. 2026/27: Deadlines and information Read more Read more Go to courses International enrollment A.Y. 2026/27 Process information and instructions: from Unigeapply to enrollment confirmation Type #1: Non-EU students with residence abroad (visa-applicant students) and non-Italian qualifications(*) > Go to dedicated page Type #2: Italian and European students (residents everywhere) with non-Italian qualification, or non-EU students regularly resident in Italy (resident students) with non-Italian qualification(*) > Go to dedicated page Type #3 : European or non-EU students with Italian qualifications > Go to the dedicated page (*)Please note: a "non-Italian" qualification means: non-Italian title obtained abroad; non-Italian title obtained in Italy; Italian title obtained abroad. Contacts Welcome Office sass@unige.it Call center open Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays, 9-11 am. Unisciti a loro e vivi la tua esperienza di mobilità in un contesto internazionale e dinamico , ideale per la tua formazione personale e professionale. Per conoscere quali attività potresti seguire durante il tuo periodo di mobilità, trova il corso di studi più simile al tuo. Leggi le attività formative previste all'interno della pagina dedicata al piano di studi dove troverai gli insegnamenti attivi, i rispettivi programmi e molte altre informazioni utili. Per aiutarti con l'italiano, UniGe ti offre la possibilità di partecipare al corso gratuito di lingua e cultura italiana per studenti stranieri . Il GEG (Gruppo Erasmus Genova) è un’associazione studentesca no-profit, parte della rete Erasmus Student Network (ESN). Il suo obiettivo è promuovere la mobilità studentesca nei progetti di scambio universitario, secondo il principio “studenti che aiutano altri studenti”. Il GEG è gestito da volontari e organizza numerose attività per accogliere gli studenti stranieri a Genova. Il GEG organizza anche un servizio di pick-up su richiesta. GEG contatti - genova@esn.it

In questa pagina trovi tutte le informazioni utili sulla procedura di candidatura per il Programma Erasmus+ e sulla vita e lo studio presso l'Università di Genova. Durata del programma La durata del soggiorno varia a seconda del corso di studi seguito nella tua università di origine e di quello che scegli di frequentare durante la tua permanenza a Genova. La durata va da un minimo di 2 mesi a un massimo di 12 mesi , in base all’accordo interistituzionale firmato tra l’università di origine e UniGe. Criteri di ammissione Tutti gli studenti Erasmus+ devono essere nominati dalla propria università nell’ambito di un accordo Erasmus+ valido. In questa pagina trovi tutte le informazioni utili sulla procedura di candidatura per il Programma Erasmus+ e sulla vita e lo studio presso l'Università di Genova. Durata del programma La durata del soggiorno varia a seconda del corso di studi seguito nella tua università di origine e di quello che scegli di frequentare durante la tua permanenza a Genova. La durata va da un minimo di 2 mesi a un massimo di 12 mesi , in base all’accordo interistituzionale firmato tra l’università di origine e UniGe. Criteri di ammissione Tutti gli studenti Erasmus+ devono essere nominati dalla propria università nell’ambito di un accordo Erasmus+ valido. Gli studenti possono essere accettati solo per i codici/ambiti ISCED inclusi nell’accordo interistituzionale sopra menzionato. Elenco delle università partner di UniGe e degli accordi Erasmus+ N.B. Se non trovi il tuo ambito di studio nell’elenco o nel modulo di candidatura, contatta o verifica con la tua università di origine. Conoscenze linguistiche consigliate Tutti gli ambiti disciplinari: ITALIANO – B1, INGLESE – B1 Medicina: ITALIANO – B1 Procedura di candidatura Il modulo di candidatura è disponibile qui: https://servizionline.unige.it/studenti/applicationform In caso di problemi tecnici durante la procedura online, scrivi a: help.applicationform@unige.it IMPORTANTE PER STUDENTI NON UE: Secondo la normativa italiana sull’immigrazione, per iscriversi e svolgere la mobilità Erasmus presso l’Università di Genova, tutti gli studenti in arrivo con cittadinanza non UE devono essere in possesso di un visto di tipo D per mobilità di studio. Sono esenti solo gli studenti già in possesso di un permesso di soggiorno esclusivamente per motivi di studio rilasciato da un paese UE. Il permesso deve coprire l’intero periodo di mobilità e deve essere in formato tessera; non sono accettati documenti di rinnovo o permessi in formato cartaceo. Tutti gli studenti, inclusi i rifugiati, sono vivamente invitati a contattare in anticipo la propria università di origine e/o il consolato italiano competente per avere informazioni sulle procedure obbligatorie.
